positive: An intrinsic source error prevents the required C++ build, corroborated by admitted source-bound diagnostics when available.
negative: Missing external judge assets, incompatible local environment, timeouts or unperformed builds alone are not source compilation defects.
overlap: Assess latent independent semantic defects separately; do not label every consequence of a compile blocker.

positive: Input parsing or required output representation is wrong: tokens, ordering, capitalization, delimiters or extra text differ from the specification.
negative: A wrong computed value alone is not an input/output-format defect when parsing and representation are correct.
overlap: Also label a separately evidenced computation defect, not every numerical mismatch.

positive: A concrete source-level predicate, arithmetic expression or state update violates required behavior.
negative: Do not add this merely because a specialized category or any wrong output exists; identify an independent wrong decision or update.
overlap: Loop/array/function/algorithm defects may coexist with logic only when a distinct predicate or state-update error supports it.

positive: Loop initialization, continuation, progress or iteration bounds cause missed, repeated or nonterminating required work.
negative: The presence of a loop or a wrong calculation inside a correctly controlled loop is insufficient.
overlap: Array or boundary labels may coexist when their own conditions hold; do not automatically add algorithm.

positive: Incorrect indexing, bounds, storage, character access or array/string mutation causes a concrete defect.
negative: Merely using an array/string, printing text or choosing a wrong high-level method is insufficient.
overlap: A faulty iteration bound can also be a loop defect; identify actual storage/index behavior.

positive: Wrong argument passing, reference/pointer propagation, return behavior, function interface or call semantics causes a defect.
negative: A function merely containing an unrelated arithmetic/loop defect is insufficient.
overlap: Label independent caller/callee computation errors separately; do not infer missing references when value passing is valid.

positive: A valid specified boundary or special case is mishandled while the intended general computation works, with an identifiable witness.
negative: An arbitrary failing input, excluded-domain input or uniformly wrong algorithm is not automatically an edge-case defect.
overlap: Boundary indexing/loop defects may share this label when the valid special-case failure is explicit.

positive: The selected computational method, recurrence or decomposition is fundamentally unsuitable, or violates an explicit required algorithm/complexity constraint.
negative: A local expression, iteration off-by-one, format defect or any wrong answer alone is insufficient.
overlap: Do not automatically stack logic/loop/algorithm; use multiple labels only for separately supported mechanisms.

positive: Fixed answers, lookup or special-cased inputs violate an explicit implementation policy or replace required general computation with unsupported fixed responses.
negative: Explicitly permitted finite-domain tables, mathematical constants and required literal output strings are not hard-code errors.
overlap: A prohibited but behaviorally correct lookup is a policy defect; do not invent functional errors. Wrong fixed answers can have independent logic defects.

positive: An explicit applicable coding-style rule is violated, or a separately documented course style policy applies.
negative: Personal formatting preferences, brevity and functionally correct code without a stated style rule are insufficient.
overlap: Style does not imply functional failure; other labels require separate evidence.
